title: Black Clover Season 2 Episode 6 Previews Noelle and Charlotte Facing Vanica
content:
Black Clover Season 2 has released preview images and synopsis for Episode 6 (Episode 176 overall) ahead of its November 7 premiere. The new season officially began on October 3, 2026 , with Crunchyroll streaming it worldwide. The anime previously revealed a special Devil Union Asta visual following Episode 3. The official Episode 6 “The Sacred Valkyrie” synopsis:

After an intense hand-to-hand battle, Magna emerged victorious against Dante!! With Dante defeated, only two members of the Dark Triad remain to be taken down in order to stop the advent of Qliphoth. One of them, Vanica, uses not only her own Blood Magic but also Curse-Warding Magic, a power granted by her devil, to control Lolopechka, whom she abducted from the Heart Kingdom, forcing her to attack Charlotte and Rill. Just then, Noelle and Gaja arrive on the scene. To counter the power of devils, Noelle has borrowed the power of the Water Spirit, Undine, and acquired a new form of magic known as “Saint Stage”!

You can see the preview images below:

The main staff for Season 2 includes:

• Director: Ayataka Tanemura

• Series Composition: Keiichiro Ochi

• Character Design: Itsuko Takeda

• Sub-Character Design: Kumiko Tokunaga

• Prop Design: Kosei Takahashi

• Music: Minako Seki

• Animation Production: Studio Pierrot

The opening song by WANIMA is titled “Kienai Riyuu” (The Reason That Won’t Disappear).

ALSO READ: Black Clover Creator Draws Toru Oikawa From Haikyu!! Black Clover Final Volume and Official Guidebook Released, Includes New 15-Page Manga by Yuki Tabata

You can also see the main visual .

The Black Clover manga was serialized in the Weekly Shonen Jump magazine from 2015 to August 2023, before transferring to Jump GIGA . It entered its final arc in August 2022 and officially ended on May 1 after eleven years of serialization. The manga is available to read on Viz Media’s website, MANGA Plus website, and the Shonen Jump mobile app in English.

It received a 170-episode anime adaptation by Studio Pierrot, which ran from 2017 to 2021. The Black Clover: Sword of the Wizard King movie premiered on June 16 and is streaming on Netflix. Crunchyroll streams the TV anime, and they describe the story:

In a world where magic is everything, Asta and Yuno are both found abandoned at a church on the same day. While Yuno is gifted with exceptional magical powers, Asta is the only one in this world without any. At the age of fifteen, both receive grimoires, magic books that amplify their holder’s magic. Asta’s is a rare Grimoire of Anti-Magic that negates and repels his opponent’s spells. Being opposite but good rivals, Yuno and Asta are ready for the hardest of challenges to achieve their common dream: to be the Wizard King. Giving up is never an option!

title: This Cult Sci-fi Movie Was Roasted by Critics 38 Years Ago, But It Changed Movies, Video Games, and Art Forever
content:
There are definitely movies that age badly. And there are films that look even better decades later. Then there’s the rare one that defies all expectations. Imagine a futuristic city filled with neon lights, motorcycle gangs, and enough government corruption to make everybody suspicious. Surprisingly, that’s still a concept that is hard to find in modern stories. Now add psychic teenagers and a military experiment that goes horribly wrong—things are about to get cooking.

Audiences in Japan got their first look at this bizarre science-fiction anime in 1988. American critics weren’t the most positive when it arrived from overseas. Some dismissed its story as confusing, while others weren’t particularly impressed by its relentless violence. The ironic thing is, plenty of filmmakers and artists saw something worth borrowing from. Its influence eventually reached Hollywood, video games, and music videos. Even people who have never watched an anime movie have probably encountered something that owes it a major debt.

Akira Was the Sci-Fi Movie American Critics Completely Misunderstood

Katsuhiro Otomo’s Akira arrived in Japanese theaters in July 1988. He adapted his own manga into a story about a futuristic Tokyo struggling to recover from disaster. The new city represents a chaotic mix of urban problems. Motorcycle gangs terrorize the streets. Politicians fight to maintain control, and the military conducts clandestine experiments that probably should have stayed behind closed doors. Two teenagers named Kaneda and Tetsuo find themselves caught up in the mix. Their new friendship takes a nasty turn when Tetsuo develops terrifying psychic abilities after being adducted and experimented on. Suddenly, the biggest threat to Neo-Tokyo isn’t another street gang. It’s a teenager who can barely control his own powers.

Early in my anime career, I watched Akira on VHS before I was old enough to fully understand it. I watched it several times, and beyond appreciating its animation and music, the characters and story truly stuck with me. The plot isn’t overly complicated; there are just so many layers to peel back and analyze. But that’s part of the movie’s appeal. I never finished buying and reading the entire manga series, but that’s going to change soon. This story is a masterpiece as both an anime and cinematic film. If you haven’t already, you need to experience this work of art.

The movie looks incredible. That’s probably the easiest way to describe it. Otomo created a futuristic city that feels crowded and alive. Its glowing advertisements and enormous buildings give Neo-Tokyo a personality of its own. The motorcycle sequences are still spectacular. The animation is packed with details that most movies wouldn’t bother attempting. More than 160,000 animation cels helped bring the film to life. American critics weren’t immediately impressed, though. When Akira reached American audiences in 1990, some reviewers found its story difficult to follow. The Los Angeles Times famously dismissed it as “High-Tech Hokum From Japan.” That’s a pretty brutal assessment for a movie that would eventually become a landmark of science-fiction storytelling.

How Akira Changed Hollywood Movies, Video Games, and Art Forever

You don’t have to look very hard to find Akira ‘s fingerprints on modern science fiction. The Wachowskis admired Japanese animation while developing The Matrix . The influence shows in the film’s futuristic atmosphere and its approach to visual storytelling. Other filmmakers followed similar paths. Even Stranger Things has played with imagery that recalls Otomo’s work. Then there’s Kanye West’s Stronger music video. Anyone familiar with Akira will recognize some of its most obvious references. It’s a little funny when you think about it. The Absolute Batman comic did an homage cover to the famous Kaneda poster. There are even rumors circulating about a live-action adaption . A Japanese animated film that confused American critics eventually became inspiration for some of Hollywood’s biggest creative projects.

Video games have embraced its world just as enthusiastically. Those towering buildings and glowing streets practically invite players to get lost in Neo-Tokyo. The motorcycle designs have become particularly recognizable, and artists still return to the movie for inspiration. You can find its influence in illustrations, fashion, and all sorts of digital artwork. But the biggest achievement might be what Akira did for animation itself. Otomo never treated the medium like something that needed to stay small or simple. He gave audiences a sprawling science-fiction epic with the ambition of a major Hollywood production. That’s another reason why the film is so important. It showed a generation of creators that animation could go almost anywhere. Critics eventually moved on to the next movie. Artists kept coming back to this one. And nearly four decades later, Neo-Tokyo still feels more alive than plenty of fictional cities that arrived long after it.

title: Reincarnation in the Game World Dan-Katsu Anime's Teaser Reveals More Cast, Theme Songs
content:
The staff for the television anime of Kaede Nishikigi 's Reincarnation in the Game World Dan-Katsu : Game Addict Plays "Encouragement for Job Hunting in Dungeons" From a "New Game" ( Game Sekai Tensei -Gamer wa [Dungeon Shūkatsu no Susume] o Play Suru- ) light novel series presented the anime's teaser promotional video, additional cast members, and theme song artists on Wednesday. MindaRyn performs the opening theme song "Play the Play," which is featured in the teaser. LINKL PLANET is performing the ending theme song "My Life Story."

The newly announced cast members are:

Ayaka Nanase as Hanna, the daughter of an alchemist and a childhood friend of Zephyrus

Kotone Izumi as Sierra, a cool beauty from a noble family

Hikaru Iida as Lana, a princess

Chihaya Asakura as Ester, Lana's guardian knight

The story centers on a gamer with the player name Zephyrus, who has played the legendary dungeon-crawl game Dungeon Shūkatsu no Susume ( Encouragement for Job Hunting in Dungeons or Dan-katsu for short) for over 8,000 hours, but he suddenly loses all his save data and dies of shock. When Zephyrus wakes up, he realizes that he is reincarnated in the unconquered world of the Dan-katsu game. He immediately gets the classic strongest job as a hero, and starts "a new game" in the world of Dan-katsu.

Yūto Uemura voices the protagonist Zephyrus.

Nagisa Miyazaki ( Negima! , Eternal Alice , Final Examination Kujira ) is directing the anime at STUDIO MASSKET . Yūji Kobayashi ( Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon Crystal: Season III , Kusunoki's Garden of Gods ) is in charge of scripts.

The anime will premiere in January 2027.

Nishikigi launched the story on the Kakuyomu website in January 2021. TO Books started publishing the novels with illustration by Shuri in March 2022. The novels' 16th volume shipped on August 15.

Hiroshi Asagi launched the novels' manga adaptation on TO Books ' Corona EX manga website in April 2022. TO Books published the manga's first compiled book volume in September 2022, and the fifth volume in October 2025.
author: ANN

title: 'Game Sekai Tensei "Dankatsu"' Reveals Additional Cast, Second Teaser Promo
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Kaede Nishikigi 's Game Sekai Tensei "Dankatsu": Gamer wa "Dungeon Shuukatsu no Susume" wo "Hajime kara" Play suru ( Reincarnation in the Game World Dankatsu: Game Addict Plays "Encouragement for Job Hunting in Dungeons" from a "New Game" ) light novel revealed additional cast and second teaser promotional video on Wednesday. The anime will premiere in January 2027.

Cast Hanna: Ayaka Nanase ( Tefuda ga Oome no Victoria ) Sierra: Kotone Izumi Lana: Hikaru Iida ( Kimi wa Meido-sama. ) Estelle: Chihaya Asakura

Nagisa Miyazaki ( Mahou Sensei Negima! ) is directing the anime at Studio Massket . Yuji Kobayashi ( Kami no Niwatsuki Kusunoki-tei ) is handling the series composition and writing the script.

Singer-songwriter MindaRyn ( Kanojo ga Koushaku-tei ni Itta Riyuu ) is performing the opening theme "Play the Play," while LINKL PLANET ( Kyoukai Senki: Kyokkou no Souki ) is performing the ending theme "My Life Story." The opening theme is previewed in the promotional video below.

Nishikigi originally began penning the action fantasy novel on the Kakuyomu website in January 2021, followed by Shousetsuka ni Narou later that same month. TO Books began printing the light novel series in March 2022, featuring illustrations by Shuri . The 16th volume was published on August 15.

A manga adaptation drawn by Hiroshi Asagi began serialization on the Corona EX website in September 2022. TO Books released the fifth volume in October 2025.

title: Promise Me the Spotlight Anime Reveals Visual, Trailer, Cast, Opening Theme Song
content:
The previously announced Promise Me the Spotlight anime adaptation revealed a key visual along with a teaser trailer featuring the cast and opening theme song. Yuika will sing the opening theme song “Nanimono demo nakatta Watashi dakara” and the announced cast consists of:

• Taihi Kimura as Koichi Okuta

• Haruna Mikawa as Mizuki Natsuno

• Mai Kanno as Awayuki Shiroi

• Yukari Anzai as Hatsune Fukuba

Seiji Kishi is directing the anime with Yuko Kakihara handling series composition. Kazuaki Morita is the character designer. Team TillDawn is animating the series.

Jun Wakatsuki writes and illustrates the manga that the anime is based on. Kodansha is publishing the manga in English on their K Manga web service, describing the story as: “If you can really make me the Center…then we can get married.” Meet Mizuki Natsuno, the least popular member of the nationally acclaimed idol group, Melty Strawberry. She has an eternal fan in Koichi Okuta, who is always pouring heart and soul into supporting her. Normally, a fan would never get to interact with their idol beyond the stage. But one thing led to another, and Koichi now finds himself living together with Mizuki in his own house. He vows to make her the new Center of Melty Strawberry, sparking an unconventional tag-team between a devoted fan and his idol. Together, they attempt to elevate Mizuki’s career from obscurity to stardom! Source: Official website © Jun Watasuki ∙ Kodansha/Watacen Production Committee

title: Butt Detective TV Anime Gets New Episodes Starting Next April
content:
The staff for the Butt Detective ( Oshiri Tantei ) anime announced on Wednesday that the anime will have new episodes that will premiere in April 2027. The staff made the announcement on November 4, which has the nickname "Nice Butt Day" ("Ii Oshiri no Hi") since "11/04" can be read as a Japanese wordplay on "ii oshi" or "nice butt." The anime's site unveiled the below visual for the anime.

The previous batch of new episodes debuted on October 3 and is currently airing.

The first three episodes of the television anime premiered on NHK Educational in May 2018, and a new series of seven episodes premiered in July 2018. The anime began a regular television anime airing in December 2018, and has been running weekly since. The latest batch of new episodes premiered in October 2025.

Eiga Oshiri Tantei: Star and Moon ( Butt Detective the Movie: Star and Moon), the third anime film for the franchise , opened in Japan in March 2025.

title: 'Watashi wo Center ni Suru to Chikaimasu ka?' Reveals Main Cast, Staff, Opening Theme, Teaser Promo
content:
The official website of the Watashi wo Center ni Suru to Chikaimasu ka? ( Promise Me the Spotlight ) television anime revealed the main cast, staff, a key visual (pictured), the opening theme, and a teaser promotional video on Wednesday. The anime series adapting Jun Wakatsuki 's idol romance manga is scheduled to air on TV Tokyo's six affiliated stations.

Cast Mizuki Natsuno: Haruna Mikawa ( Ore dake Level Up na Ken ) Kouichi Okuta: Taihi Kimura ( Onmyou Kaiten Re:Birth ) Awayuki Shiroi: Mai Kanno ( Idoly Pride ) Hatsune Fukuba: Yukari Anzai ( Lapis Re:LiGHTs )

Staff Director: Seiji Kishi ( Angel Beats! , Ao no Orchestra ) Series Composition: Yuuko Kakihara ( Orange , Ao no Hako ) Character Design: Kazuaki Morita ( Ansatsu Kyoushitsu , Tsuki ga Kirei ) Studio: Team TillDawn

Singer-songwriter Yuika is performing the opening theme "Nanimono demo Nakatta Watashi dakara," which was previewed in the teaser promotional video below.

Wakatsuki began drawing the idol romance manga in Shounen Magazine Edge in November 2022. Following the magazine's discontinuation in 2023, it was transferred to the Magazine pocket app in February 2024. Kodansha published the sixth volume on July 9.

The series was published in English through the K Manga platform on February 24.

title: Promise Me the Spotlight Anime Unveils Teaser, Main Cast, Staff
content:
Bandai Namco Filmworks revealed on Wednesday the teaser trailer, key visual, main cast, and main staff members for the television anime of Jun Wakatsuki 's Promise Me the Spotlight ( Watashi o Center ni Suru to Chikaimasuka? ) manga. The company also revealed that the anime will air on TV Tokyo and its six affiliate channels.

The anime will star:

Haruna Mikawa as Mizuki "Zukki" Natsuno, the least popular but a hardworking member of the famous idol group Melty Strawberry, who is known for her stern expression and being curt

Taihi Kimura as Kōichi Okuta, a high school student and Mizuki's die-hard fan

But one thing led to another, and Koichi now finds himself living together with Mizuki in his own house. He vows to make her the new Center of Melty Strawberry, sparking an unconventional tag-team between a devoted fan and his idol. Together, they attempt to elevate Mizuki's career from obscurity to stardom!

title: Pero Pero★Sparkles Anime Reveals Cast, Staff, January Debut
content:
The official website for the television anime of Yurie Sekiya 's Pero Pero★Sparkles characters revealed the cast, staff, January premiere on TV Tokyo , and a new key visual for the anime on Wednesday.

The cast includes:

• Yuki Sakakihara as Mero

• Mai Kanno as Kyun

• Ai Fairouz as Ru

• Yōhei Azakami as Narrator

Mao Miyashita is directing the anime at Usagiou , and Yūji Umoto is in charge of the series scripts. Shiomi Yano is designing the characters, while Yui Ōzaki is the art director. Saya Fukase is directing the sound, and Shōta Kowashi is composing the music with TV Tokyo Music producing the music.

Sekiya launched the characters in 2013, and the characters have since spawned merchandise, as well as a 2020 YouTube anime.

title: Kemono Jihen Manga's Climax Is 'Imminent'
content:
The December issue of Shueisha 's Jump SQ. magazine confirmed on Wednesday that the story climax of Shō Aimoto 's Kemono Jihen manga is "imminent."

The 25th compiled book volume, which shipped on August 4, announced that the series will end in the next volume.

Seven Seas Entertainment publishes the manga in English and describes the story:

Inugami is a Tokyo detective who specializes in the occult. One day, answering a call to a remote village leads him to Dorotabo: a peculiar boy nicknamed after a yokai that haunts muddy rice paddies. The boy has no parents and is somewhat unnerving, emitting a foul odor that draws the ire of those around him. Inugami, however, quickly realizes that there's something more monstrous about Dorotabo than just his nickname–a fact proven when the two of them investigate an inhuman creature attacking local livestock. Perhaps Inugami can take this mistreated boy under his wing and train him to face the secret, supernatural beasts hidden in the world...using the eerie powers of his own body.

Aimoto launched the manga in Jump SQ. in December 2016. Seven Seas released the 22nd volume in English on October 6. The manga inspired a television anime that premiered in January 2021.

The series took a one-issue break in September following the death of Aimoto's brother in August.

The series took a one-issue break in February. Aimoto shared that she had gastroenteritis at the beginning of the year. Aimoto added that she is feeling better now and will also get an endoscopy soon.
author: ANN
